Load packages and the data
```{R}
library(devtools)
load_all('/home/salbalkus/Research/RieszCML/')

library(nadir)
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
# read in data via readr::read_csv
wash <- read_csv(
  paste0(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tlverse/tlverse-data/master/",
    "wash-benefits/washb_data.csv"
  )
)
```

Let's look at the Bangladesh Wash Benefits study data. We are interested in the effect of maternal age (`momage`) on the outcome of weight-for-height Z-scores (`whz`). Note that maternal age is not a discrete variable, so we need to consider an estimand appropriate for this. We will consider a modified treatment policy $A + 1$. 
```{R}
head(wash)
```

Let's define a way to estimate this estimand for the entire dataset.
```{R}
df = wash %>% select(momage, momedu, momheight, Nlt18, watmin, hfiacat, tr, whz) %>%
              rename(Y = whz) %>%
              mutate(value = 1) %>% 
              pivot_wider(names_from = tr, 
                          values_from = value, 
                          values_fill = 0) %>%
              drop_na()
```

```{R}
#---------------------------------------------
# Stage 1 RieszCurve:
#   parameter is E[Y | L1, A1] under intervention A2 = 1
#---------------------------------------------
rc1 <- function(delta, treatment){return(RieszCurve$new(
  nuis = function(data) {
    # regression for Y given current history
    m_fit <- glm(Y ~ momage + momedu + momheight + watmin + hfiacat + get(treatment) + Nlt18,
                 family = gaussian(),
                 data = data)

    data_shift <- data %>% mutate(momage = momage + delta, "{treatment}" := 1)

    # treatment mechanism for A2
    g_fit <- glm(get(treatment) ~ momage + momedu + momheight + watmin + hfiacat + Nlt18,
                 family = binomial(),
                 data = data)

    list(
      m = predict(m_fit, newdata = data, type = "response"),
      m1 = predict(m_fit, newdata = data_shift, type = "response"),
      invprop = data[[treatment]] / predict(g_fit, newdata = data, type = "response")
    )
  },
  h = ~ m1,
  f = ~ m,
  alpha = ~ invprop,
  ic_expr = ~ h + alpha * (Y - f)
))}

#---------------------------------------------
# Stage 2 RieszCurve:
#   parameter is E[h[j=1] | L1] under intervention A1 = 1
#---------------------------------------------
rc2 <- function(delta){return(RieszCurve$new(
  nuis = function(data) {
    m_fit <- glm(`h[j=1]` ~ momage + momedu + momheight + watmin + hfiacat,
                 family = gaussian(),
                 data = data)

    data_shift <- data
    data_shift$momage <- data_shift$momage + delta

    # Fit the probabilistic classifier from Diaz et al. (2021)
    data_aug <- rbind(cbind(data, I = 0), cbind(data_shift, I = 1))
    r_fit <- glm(I ~ momage + momedu + momheight + watmin + hfiacat,
                 family = binomial(),
                 data = data_aug)

    list(
      m = predict(m_fit, newdata = data, type = "response"),
      m1 = predict(m_fit, newdata = data_shift, type = "response"),
      r = predict(r_fit, newdata = data_shift, type = "response")
    )
  },
  h = ~ m1,
  f = ~ m,
  alpha = ~ r / (1 - r),
  ic_expr = ~ h + alpha * (`h[j=1]` - f)
))}

#---------------------------------------------
# Compose the two stages
#---------------------------------------------
rc_composed <- function(delta, treatment){return(ComposedRieszCurve$new(
  rc_list = list(rc1(delta, treatment), rc2(delta))
))}

#---------------------------------------------
# One-step estimate using composed object
#---------------------------------------------
est_onestep <- riesz_estimate(
  data = df,
  rc = rc_composed(0, "WSH"),
)

est_onestep

#---------------------------------------------
# TMLE using the composed object
#---------------------------------------------
est_tmle <- riesz_tmle(
  data = df,
  rc = rc_composed(3, "Control"),
  fluctuation = "logistic",
  bounds = c(min(df$Y), max(df$Y)),
  outcome_col = "Y"
)


# Run a bunch of them
get_estimate <- function(treatment){
  est_tmle <- riesz_tmle(
    data = df,
    rc = rc_composed(3, treatment),
    fluctuation = "logistic",
    bounds = c(min(df$Y), max(df$Y)),
    outcome_col = "Y"
  )
  data.frame(est = est_tmle$estimate, low = est_tmle$ci_low, high = est_tmle$ci_high, cat = treatment)

}

result <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(wash$tr), get_estimate))


p <- ggplot(result) + 
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(wash$whz)), color = "darkgray") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high, y = cat, color = cat)) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = est, y = cat, color = cat)) + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position="none") + ylab("") + xlab("Estimate")

ggsave("wash.png", p, width = 5, height = 5)
```
